title: Stochastic process model of rough surface contact
abstract: The stochastic process model of rough surface contact, widely known as Persson's theory of contact, serves as a representative multi-scale model that has been extensively applied across various fields of tribology. In this chapter, we briefly introduce the background of the development of Persson's theory of contact. We thoroughly discuss Persson's theory for purely normal elastic contact, with a special focus on solving the probability density of the contact pressure and the interfacial gap using partial differential equations. Subsequent applications of these fundamental results in addressing more complex interfacial properties in other fields of tribology are also examined. Finally, several recommendations regarding future studies of Persson's theory are proposed. This review article is expected to assist researchers in quickly familiarizing themselves with the current state of the art of Persson's theory and to attract more attention from tribologists and solid mechanicians, thereby contributing to the development and application of Persson's theory of contact.
summary: This review article thoroughly examines Persson's theory for modeling contact mechanics between rough surfaces. It details how the stochastic nature of surface roughness is incorporated by deriving a differential equation that governs the evolution of the contact pressure probability density function with increasing magnification scale. The work aims to provide researchers with a comprehensive understanding of this state-of-the-art multi-scale theoretical framework.
main_problem: The primary problem is modeling tribological phenomena arising from rough surface contact by integrating the multi-scale nature of surface texture into contact mechanics theory.
main_result: The paper details Persson's theory, which develops a differential equation describing how the probability density function (PDF) of contact pressure evolves deterministically with increasing magnification ($\zeta$).
method: The methodology involves characterizing rough topography using stochastic processes and solving partial differential equations to track the evolution of the contact pressure PDF.
model_or_system: The system is the contact between two uncorrelated rough surfaces. The model centers on Persson's theory, treating the variation as a Markov process whose statistics are governed by diffusion-like equations.
key_observables: Interfacial gap, real area of contact, interfacial contact stiffness, and the magnification-dependent Probability Density Function (PDF) of contact pressure $P(p, \zeta)$.
important_parameters: Magnification $\zeta = \lambda_l/\lambda_s$, upper cut-off wavelength ($\lambda_l$), lower cut-off wavelength ($\lambda_s$).
main_assumptions: The roughness is assumed to be random, bandwidth-limited, self-affine, and isotropic. Key assumptions include that the pressure variation follows a Markov process.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the Power Spectral Density (PSD) of rough topography across various length scales and map the historical development of multi-scale contact models leading up to Persson's theory.
paper_structure: The review first introduces the background of Persson's theory, thoroughly discusses its application to purely normal elastic contact by solving the PDF evolution via PDEs, examines subsequent applications in other tribological fields, and concludes with recommendations for future research directions.
why_interesting: While focused on classical mechanics, the rigorous use of stochastic processes (stochastic differential equations) to model system evolution based on scale separation ($\zeta$) shares mathematical parallels with analyzing open quantum systems or complex many-body dynamics where coarse-graining is necessary.
